workload_note: Single-record calls: native HTTP _update versus one-record Weir SDK Mutate; three causal phases (reconcile, product, parallel sellers), four OS processes and 128 total goroutine workers. Application-call attempts are measured client invocation counters, not backend wire commands. HTTP-observer backend request/byte metrics remain unavailable.
cpu_note: Sampled CPU only, weighted by covered time; not extrapolated to unsampled intervals. Rejected arrivals have no completed latency. All rows and negative ratios are retained; comparisons are within one workflow run.
qualification_note: Formal measurement validates source/audit, duration, rounds, error-free dispatched business work and CPU coverage. Formal all-arrivals applies only to fixed-rate rows and additionally rejects dropped arrivals, excess latency, drain and generator lag. Fixed-rate results do not establish maximum throughput capacity.
http_note: Disabled observers provide no backend HTTP request/byte counts; those values remain null. Native HTTP call attempts are directly instrumented client calls; Weir Mutate calls do not measure backend HTTP command counts.
cleanup_note: Cleanup receipts attest only the final owned process and removed database container. Earlier server replacement waits synchronously in ReplaceServer/stopProcess; there is no separate historical OS termination receipt.
comparison_note: A lower-database-CPU/comparable-completion claim requires both paths to pass every all-arrivals gate in all three paired rounds, each QPS ratio within [0.95, 1.05], and CPU ms/completed product lower in each round. Ratios are within one workflow runner only; no cross-run CPU/QPS pooling or confidence interval is calculated.
